correctness.rationale: For n≥5 the real moment-angle polyhedral product X_n=(D¹,S⁰)^{C_n} is a connected closed orientable surface with cubical cells 2^n,n2^{n−1},n2^{n−2} and χ=(4−n)2^{n−2}. Coordinate rotations preserve the coherent square-orientation cycle; reflections reverse it. No nontrivial rotation can preserve a nonempty face of C_n, so rotation-fixed sets are precisely 2^{gcd(n,a)} periodic sign vectors. Each reflection fixed set consists of disjoint circles (boundary squares in two nonadjacent exceptional coordinate orbits), hence has χ=0 and supplies mirror arcs. Finite local stabilizers act on a circle link as rotation/reflection: ordinary quotient is a compact connected surface with boundary. Burnside χ=(1/(2n))[(4−n)2^{n−2}+∑_{k=1}^{n−1}2^{gcd(n,k)}] yields wedge of r=1+2^{n−3}−(1/(2n))∑_{d|n}φ(d)2^{n/d} circles. For odd n, rotation conjugacy makes X^s→(X/C_n)^{sbar} a bijection (because 2 invertible mod n), giving 2^{(n−3)/2} boundary circles. Independently counted full equivariantly diagonally triangulated cell orbit Euler for n5…10, obtaining χ=0,−1,−6,−14,−34,−74 and corresponding ranks 1,2,7,15,35,75.
